searchText: <@199561711278227457> today something interesting came up in a discussion. You still have forkchoice dumps taken regularly right? I was wandering if you have the infra in place to record any attestation for an invalid block in mainnet? It'd be nice to save automatically such objects - blocks whose parents are bad blocks - attestations to bad block roots If you aren't doing this yet I think your monitoring infra should be doing this. I can help modding a Prysm client to do this if you want We have a tool called Hermes, basically a tracing node on the p2p layer built by the probe labs team. I think that could be up for the job, right <@84562395988508672> or <@181594452228308992> ? Wouldn't be surprised if we're already collecting the data Yeah I was hoping that you'd say that. If that is the case, I'd love to see if you have attestations for the last invalid blocks in mainnet, we've had a few They're both in the aussie timezone. So should have an answer for you in a few hours 😄 is there a project that tries to build a compiler from rust to EVM? This is not particularly feasible because many EVM concepts don't translate well to general purpose languages and there isn't much benefit to it Alternatively, have you used Fe? I was thinking it would be nice to have certain cryptography libraries available for EVM without having to reimplement them. But seems like this is not feasible 🤷‍♂️ No, what’s that? https://fe-lang.org/ although it seems github pages is down I think they are, not all of em but many https://www.rareskills.io/post/solidity-precompiles

excerpts.content: <@199561711278227457> today something interesting came up in a discussion. You still have forkchoice dumps taken regularly right? I was wandering if you have the infra in place to record any attestation for an invalid block in mainnet?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
It'd be nice to save automatically such objects
- blocks whose parents are bad blocks 
- attestations to bad block roots
If you aren't doing this yet I think your monitoring infra should be doing this. I can help modding a Prysm client to do this if you want

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: We have a tool called Hermes, basically a tracing node on the p2p layer built by the probe labs team. I think that could be up for the job, right <@84562395988508672> or <@181594452228308992> ? Wouldn't be surprised if we're already collecting the data

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Yeah I was hoping that you'd say that. If that is the case, I'd love to see if you have attestations for the last invalid blocks in mainnet, we've had a few

excerpts.author: parithosh
